core.title: Every acceptance makes an explicit telemetry decision
core.given: Telemetry is adopted: the telemetry root (the tracking plan's root) exists, or any acceptance declares telemetry (either alone suffices).
core.when: You plan or review any acceptance or tracking-plan item.
core.then: Every acceptance declares an explicit telemetry decision: disposition `required` listing at least one well-formed, concrete telemetry URN that the acceptance demands be observed emitted and that exists as a tracking-plan item in the tracking plan, or disposition `not-applicable` with a rationale of at least 20 characters.
prefer: Record the decision explicitly: disposition required listing concrete telemetry URNs taken from the tracking plan, or disposition not-applicable with a considered rationale of at least 20 characters.
List required items by kind (events, metrics, traces, logs).
Treat not-applicable as a considered answer, not the absence of one.
Make every acceptance a tracking-plan item names resolve to a declared acceptance.
avoid: Omitting the telemetry declaration once adopted — silence is not a disposition.
Malformed, non-concrete or unplanned URNs (the requirement is unplannable).
Token rationales under 20 characters that are not a real answer.
Requiring a test for every debug log or internal span.
Forcing acceptance lists and plan references to mirror each other.
unless: Diagnostic logs and internal spans are not automatically telemetry obligations; the decision is per acceptance.
Inert until adoption: no telemetry root and no acceptance telemetry declaration → nothing emitted (see the tracking-plan schema rule in this rulebook).
core.why: An explicit per-acceptance decision removes the false choice between testing every debug log and having no observability requirement; both-direction resolution keeps traceability intact.
evidence: Every acceptance has a telemetry declaration with disposition required or not-applicable.
Each required declaration lists ≥1 URN; each is well-formed, concrete, and resolves to a tracking-plan item in the tracking plan.
Each not-applicable declaration carries a rationale of ≥20 characters.
Every acceptance reference in a tracking-plan item resolves to a declared acceptance.
The stack's convention check for this rule (acceptance telemetry decisions and tracking-plan resolution) reports no findings.
verification: Adoption gate: the check is active if the telemetry root exists — an existing root counts even when it contains no plan items yet — OR any acceptance declares telemetry; it emits nothing only if there is no telemetry root and no acceptance telemetry declaration. Presence of tracking-plan items is not required for the acceptance checks.

Decision = disposition plus, for required, concrete item lists by kind (events, metrics, traces, logs); for not-applicable, a rationale of at least 20 characters. A missing or invalid disposition, or an empty required list, is a finding.

A required item is a concrete telemetry URN the acceptance demands be observed emitted; it must exist as a tracking-plan item in the tracking plan (the telemetry root is a profile path whose existence alone adopts the capability; items are located by scanning beneath that root via the plan-artifact kinds; URN well-formedness per the tracking-plan schema rule).

Resolution is checked in both directions (acceptance → plan URNs, plan item → acceptance references); the lists are not required to be mirror images, because an item may serve acceptances beyond those that first required it.
Strict disposition: the check fails on every finding; there is no advisory mode and no ratchet baseline. Severity 2 on the rulebook's scale.

The concrete telemetry-declaration construct comes from the profile (the stack's telemetry-decision idiom); the concrete detector/validator and finding ids of this rule are realization details of the stack's checker.

values: telemetry root (the tracking plan exists in the repository)

fires: Telemetry is adopted and any acceptance in the repository (new or existing, untouched) has no telemetry declaration — including when no tracking-plan items exist yet.
An acceptance declares disposition missing or other than required / not-applicable.
An acceptance declares required with an empty list (zero URNs).
An acceptance declares required with a URN that is malformed, non-concrete, or absent from the tracking plan.
An acceptance declares not-applicable with no rationale or a rationale under 20 characters.
A tracking-plan item (including in tracking-plan-only changes, or when no acceptance declares telemetry) references an acceptance that no acceptance declares.
doesNotFire: No telemetry root exists and no acceptance declares telemetry (capability not adopted).
A tracking-plan item serves acceptances beyond those that list it as required (lists need not mirror).
Diagnostic logs or internal spans that no acceptance requires have no dedicated test.

profileRequirements.meaning: Root of the telemetry tracking plan and signal definitions, as a path: the tree under which tracking-plan items live. Existence of this root is adoption alternative A — an existing root activates the rule even when it contains no plan items yet — and it is the resolution target for required telemetry URNs and the source of reverse-direction acceptance references. Plan items are found by a descendant scan derived from this root (the Bun realization derives the glob `<telemetry root>/**` from it). The frozen Bun sidecar carries only the placeholder root.
The concrete artifact kinds that play the 'tracking-plan item' role in this stack, so the check can enumerate plan items, their URNs and their acceptance references.

The concrete construct by which an acceptance declares its explicit telemetry decision: disposition required with a list of concrete telemetry URNs by kind, or disposition not-applicable with a rationale. The core obligates the decision content; each stack supplies this declaration idiom.
profileRequirements.bunValue: Shape: `telemetry: {disposition: required, events: [<concrete telemetry:event:… URN from the tracking plan>]}` or `telemetry: {disposition: not-applicable, rationale: <considered reason, ≥20 chars>}`.

bunOnly.reason: Names this rule's concrete validator id; detector/validator ids are realization details, so the core's evidence names the check generically.

bunOnly.text: path_glob fact with value `<telemetry root>/**`, checked directly by the validator planner_telemetry_plan.
bunOnly.reason: The path-glob fact form and the descendant-matching scan glob `<telemetry root>/**` are the realization's mechanism (the derived scan beneath the profile's telemetry root); the core states adoption alternative A as the telemetry root's presence, with the root path supplied by the existing profile key roots.telemetry — an existing empty root still activates the rule.

Adoption gate carried into core:verification, neutralized; 'presence of tracking-plan items is not required' preserved, and an existing (even empty) telemetry root adopts the capability.
Decision definition and finding conditions carried in meaning.

neutralityNotes: The rule is artifact-content-level, so nearly everything was already neutral. The telemetry root is represented by the dedicated profile key roots.telemetry (path; Bun value `<telemetry root>`); the descendant scan glob `<telemetry root>/**` is the realization's mechanism (bunOnly), so an existing empty root still activates the rule. The concrete telemetry-declaration shape is exposed through the map key idiom.acceptance_schema#telemetry_decision (entry telemetry_decision); the application-specific example URN and rationale stay only in the Bun audit trail. 'tracking-plan item' binds via roles.plan_artifact.kinds (Bun value "tracking-plan item"); 'acceptance' needs no path or suffix value because the frozen sidecar asserts none. URN well-formedness is delegated to the tracking-plan schema rule, referenced generically. The validator id planner_telemetry_plan and the shared policy node id are realization details; severity 2 and strict disposition are carried in core:verification.
